movedToNotes: B1 · These are Korea's national zero-energy building (ZEB) grades, run by MOLIT (Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport). Seoul's climate plan builds on them.
B2 · What the grades measure: energy self-sufficiency, the share of its own energy a building produces itself. Grade 5 is 20 to 40%, Grade 1 is over 100%.
B2 · Seoul's own plan for new public buildings: Grade 5 now, Grade 4 by 2030, Grade 3 by 2050.
B3 · Public first (2020, Grade 5 in 2023), private after. Private rule planned for 2024, delayed one year after the construction industry pushed back.
B3 · Mention that sources give slightly different rollout dates.

B3 · Read this word for word (Hong Seongjun, head of MOLIT's Green Building Division): "improving the energy performance of private buildings, which account for the majority of buildings, is an essential task"
B3 · If asked: no confirmed % for grades 4 to 2 · private apartment rule is 13% in one source, 40% in another · 2030 goal is less certain · no source gives the Energy Dream Center a grade.
B3 · Next: photo pair, Seoul City Hall and P.S. 62, two public buildings. Then the Energy Dream Center, which makes as much energy as it uses in a year.

For the study guide (dossier 3.2), the detail behind the s09 "If asked" note: the sources give no confirmed percentages for grades 4 to 2. For new private apartments, one source says they must make at least 13% of their own energy, and another says 40% self-sufficiency for complexes of 30 or more units; they seem to be different measures, or one is a later revision. The 2030 goal (all new buildings in Korea to be ZEB) is reported but less certain. No source gives the Energy Dream Center a ZEB grade, so don't call it Grade 1.

movedToNotes: B1 · Name, date and place: Seoul Energy Dream Center, opened 2012 in World Cup Park, Mapo-gu, on top of the old Nanjido landfill. Korea's first zero-energy public building.
B1 · Designed by a German and Korean team led by Fraunhofer ISE, for the Seoul city government.
B1 · If asked about Gerkan Marg & Partners: some sites credit them, I couldn't confirm it.
B2 · The ground: the landfill waste cannot carry the building's weight.
B3 · So piles go down through the waste to solid ground, and the building sits on a reinforced concrete base plate.
B4 · The shape: square plan, three floors that get wider as they rise, each turned 45° (a pinwheel look with slanted outer walls). The shape is meant to cut energy demand.
B5 · The wings: wedge-shaped roof edges that shade the windows, shelter the entrance and hold solar panels.
B5 · White marble facade reflects sunlight (one source says about 60%).
B6 · Solar panels on the roof, the wings and a small patch of ground cover the full yearly demand, about 280,000 kWh. It stays connected to the grid. Geothermal does heating and cooling.
B6 · Over 70% less energy than a similar ordinary building. That is a reported figure.
B6 · Certified by KGBC (Korea's green building certification) and the Building Energy Efficiency Label. Envelope designed to Passive House standards.
B6 · Passive House is a German standard for very well insulated, airtight buildings that need very little heating or cooling.
B6 · The program: a public exhibition and education center about energy.

movedToNotes: B1 · Name, date and place: Nowon Energy Zero House (EZ House), Nowon-gu, Seoul. Korea's first zero-energy apartment complex. Finished September 2017, residents moved in from November 2017.
B1 · Net zero means it makes as much energy as it uses over a year. Say it aims for net zero. The reported figure is 75 to 80% of its own energy.

B2 · The exploded view: ordinary building parts, carefully layered. Bottom to top: geothermal field, structure, Passive House envelope (insulation, airtight layer, triple glazing), heat recovery ventilation, solar panels.
B3 · How it got built: a national research program run by MOLIT with Seoul and Nowon-gu. Point out who was involved: the national government, the city, the district, companies and universities.
B3 · August 2018: Building 102 became the first Korean housing to earn German Passive House certification.
B4 · The 75 to 80% self-sufficiency and the up to 61% lower energy costs (compared with similar ordinary apartments) are reported figures.
B4 · President Moon Jae-in visited in December 2017, called it Korea's first zero-energy apartment complex and used it to start a national expansion push.
B5 · LL97 limit for big apartment buildings (over 25,000 sq ft) drops by about half in 2030.
B5 · Then ask: "What would a NYCHA version of this building look like?"
B5 · NYCHA is the New York City Housing Authority, the city's public housing.
B5 · To answer it, look at who pays for it and who builds it, along with the design.

B5 · If asked: cost figures don't agree, so give none · energy costs are up to 61% lower (the 100% claim is weakly sourced) · panel counts vary, so give the range · my sources don't say if NYCHA must meet this limit.

flags: For the study guide (general knowledge): heat recovery ventilation means the fresh air coming in is warmed or cooled by the stale air going out, so little heat is lost.

For the study guide (dossier 6.2): panel counts differ between sources. UNESCAP gives 1,284 panels and 130 geothermal heat pumps; another source gives 1,800 panels. The slide uses about 1,300 to 1,800 panels plus about 130 heat pumps.

For the study guide (dossier 6.2 and the appendix): don't give a construction cost. Published figures are US$4.5M, about US$18M and about US$49M in different sources, so if asked, say they don't agree. Don't claim a 100% cut in energy costs. That claim comes from one weakly sourced government-linked presentation. Use up to 61% lower.
For the study guide: don't use the old figure of 48% (residential share of New York's building emissions) from the earlier slide. It isn't in the dossier.
For the study guide: don't say NYCHA has to meet this exact LL97 limit. The dossier doesn't say which limits apply to NYCHA buildings.

For the study guide only (dossier 8.2), the exact LL97 figures behind "drops by about half in 2030": the limit for multifamily buildings over 25,000 sq ft is 0.00675 t CO₂e per sq ft a year in 2024 to 2029 and about 0.00335 (0.003346640) in 2030 to 2034, a 50.4% drop. These numbers stay off the slide and out of the speaker notes.

movedToNotes: B1 · Both buildings were finished in 2017 and both are LEED Gold.
B1 · LEED is the US Green Building Council's green building rating. Gold is the second highest of four levels: Certified, Silver, Gold, Platinum.
B2 · Amorepacific HQ: David Chipperfield Architects, Arup on building services. Won a 2010 competition, built from 2014, finished 2017. The company has been on this site since 1956.
B2 · Cube around a central courtyard, shaped for natural air flow and daylight. Three big openings, called hanging gardens, bring light and air deep inside. Fins on the facade cut sun and glare.
B2 · LEED Gold 2018 (Core & Shell: base building only). Use about 22 floors and 7,000 to 8,000 people.

B3 · Lotte World Tower: Kohn Pedersen Fox, 555 m, 123 floors, one of the tallest buildings in the world. One source reports it as the first building over 100 floors to get LEED Gold. The form draws on Korean ceramics, porcelain and calligraphy.

B3 · Lotte equipment: 720 geothermal wells about 200 m deep, Han River water used for heating and cooling, wind turbines near the top, solar panels, energy recovery wheels, greywater reuse, rainwater harvesting.
B3 · Energy recovery wheel: moves heat from outgoing air to incoming air. Greywater: used sink and shower water, reused for things like flushing toilets.
B3 · If asked: say "solar panels, and one source says some are built into the facade". For the turbines say "vertical-axis turbines near the top". Sources disagree on the type.
B4 · Amorepacific saves energy mostly through its shape (courtyard, openings, fins), while Lotte relies mostly on added equipment.
B5 · CIBSE Building Performance Award: CIBSE (the UK body for building services engineers) judges measured performance, so the award shows Amorepacific works in use.
B5 · "LEED Gold rates Lotte against a standard building of the same kind. A 555 meter tower still has a huge amount of embodied carbon and uses a lot of energy per person."
B5 · Embodied carbon: the carbon released to make materials like concrete and steel and to build with them.

flags: For the i09 notes (photo pair right after s09; Seoul City Hall and P.S. 62), moved here from the old s12 aside. Two bullets under B1 · Seoul: "Seoul City Hall, 2012, iArc Architects. About 28% of its energy from renewables (city figure). Double-skin glass facade, 1,516 m² green wall over 7 floors." and "Criticized for the glass wave over the preserved 1926 building."

For the study guide (dossier 6.3): Seoul City Hall gets about 28.3% of its energy from solar panels, solar thermal and geothermal (the city's own figure; Wikipedia says over 25%). A double-skin facade is two layers of glass with an air gap between them. The green wall is 1,516 m² and runs from floor 1 to floor 7.

For the study guide (dossier 6.5): size figures conflict. One source gives 216,000 m² and 30 floors, another gives 22 floors above ground plus 7 basement levels. Occupants are 7,000 in one source and 8,000 in another. Use about 22 floors above ground and 7,000 to 8,000 people.
For the study guide (general knowledge): LEED Core & Shell rates the base building (structure, envelope and central systems) and leaves out the tenant interiors.

For the study guide: CIBSE is the Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers, the UK professional body for engineers who design heating, cooling and lighting systems. Its Building Performance Award is judged on measured performance.

For the study guide (general knowledge): an energy recovery wheel is a turning wheel that passes heat from outgoing air to incoming air. Greywater is used water from sinks and showers, reused for things like flushing toilets.

For the study guide (dossier 6.4): LEED rates a building against a standard building of the same type, so it measures relative efficiency. A 555 m tower's embodied carbon and energy use per person stay very large whatever its rating.
For the study guide: the notes no longer say what Amorepacific makes. If the guide mentions that it is a Korean cosmetics company, mark it as general knowledge; the dossier doesn't say it.
